title: Follow Up Boss and the handoff

steps.text: Ana books a tour. She forgets to write it down. The agent never knows. The buyer waits alone. Ouch.
Not in Follow Up Boss? It did not happen.
steps.sub: Nobody heard your call. They only see your notes.

steps.h: Smart Lists are your to-do lists. Tap each one

cards.back: Ready to buy or sell within 30 days.
Calls and texts you promised for today.
A month or two away. Friendly check-ins.

steps.h: Put the Smart Lists in order

steps.q: You are calling nurture leads. A new lead arrives. What now?
options: Finish the whole nurture list first
Finish this call, then dial the new lead
steps.why: New leads always come first. Dial within 180 seconds.

steps.text: After every talk, write a note. Always the same six parts. Then any agent can read it fast.

cards.back: What happened. Example: Call, connected, 4 minutes.
Appointment, Location, Motivation. Three parts you know!
What happens next, and who does it.

steps.h: Where does it go in the note?

options: Tue 10:42. Call, connected. A: Sat 11. L: Mesa. M: lease ends May. Next: send invite.
steps.why: It has all six parts. Facts only.

steps.text: Write about the home, not the person.
steps.sub: Fair housing: log what they want, not who they are.

steps.h: Can you write it in a note?

items.text: Needs a yard for a dog

steps.h: You booked it! Now three fast steps
steps.text: Do them before your next call. Change the stage. Send the calendar invite. Set the reminders.

steps.before: After booking, change the stage to

steps.h: What goes in the calendar invite?

cards.back: The agent opens the lead's story in one tap.
One 24 hours before. One 1 hour before.
For tours only. It tells the agent to handle it.

steps.q: When do you put the appointment on the calendar?
options: At the end of the shift
steps.why: You may forget later. Do it right away.

steps.text: Before a tour, the agent needs a signed buyer agreement. It is a paper between buyer and agent. The agent sends and explains it. Never you.

steps.says: Do I have to sign something before the tour?

options.text: Yes. I will email it to you now.
options.why: You never send it. The agent does.

options.text: No, do not worry about that.
options.why: Not true. The agent needs it signed.

options.text: Great question for your agent. Daniel will explain it before the tour.
options.why: Short and true. The agent handles it.

steps.text: Sometimes the agent is free right now. You bring the agent into the call. The lead meets the agent through you.

items: Ask the lead if the agent can join
Put the lead on a short hold
Tell the agent the lead's story
Join the calls and introduce them

steps.h: Say the handoff line out loud
steps.line: Daniel, I have Priya on the phone. She wants a 3-bed in Phoenix by May. Priya, meet Daniel, our local expert!

steps.q: The agent does not answer the handoff. What do you do?
options: Go back and book a time with two choices
steps.why: Never leave a lead waiting. Book a time.

steps.text: Booked? Stage, invite, reminders. Right away.
steps.sub: Then the agent is ready and the lead shows up.

steps.text: Great job! You can now log a call and hand off a lead.

options: Date/Time, Disposition, A, L, M, Next Step

quiz.q: What is the stage after you book an appointment?
quiz.explain: Pending Handoff tells the agent a lead is ready.

quiz.q: Who sends and explains the buyer agreement?
Which reminders go with the calendar invite?
quiz.explain: Two reminders help the lead show up.
